text.p: The following are top headlines from selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Ministry closings cause chaos: Locked doors, lost payments, busy signals greet clients of Ontario's Family Support Plan.
- U.S. readies new hit on Iraq: Missile attempt angers Pentagon.
- 5 deaths at B.C. farm called murders: Arrests in Chilliwack incident made earlier at same Fraser Valley house.
- GST break won't help literacy, Finance Minister Paul Martin says: Ottawa seeks other means than tax exemption to promote books, reading.
- Belgians reeling as murder cases snowball: News of political involvement, police bungling adds to revulsion gripping quiet country.
- Molson hunting for beer deals: Will put C$400 million 'surplus' into breweries, not dividends or buybacks, new CEO says.

- Beeg Maks on a roll: It's been six years since McDonald's opened its first outlet in Russia. Despite competition from a local chain, business is booming. It's so good the company has accelerated expansion plans.
- Bond trading counts for less in dealers' revenue: More competition, less business cited.
- Ottawa to lift ban on PCB exports to U.S.
- Cable TV without the cable set for launch: Brandon, Manitoba-based SkyCable Inc said yesterday it is just days away from launching the world's first 'wireless cable' service.

- Poco Petroleum deal may spur new batch of mergers: A C$225 million takeover bid for Gardiner Oil & Gas Ltd by Poco could be the catalyst for a new bout of merger mania on the oilpatch. - Sherritt risks U.S. ire with Cuba meeting:

Sherritt International, the Canadian company whose executives are excluded from the U.S. under the Helms-Burton law, will hold a board meeting in Cuba tomorrow in a clear signal to U.S. authorities it intends to maintain its investments on the communist-ruled island.
